h1: What does Massachusetts law say about municipal setbacks for ADUs?
title: Massachusetts ADU Setback Protections: State Law and Local Zoning
description: Understand why state ADU law does not erase local dimensional rules and how the protected-use standard applies.
short_answer: Massachusetts law protects a single ADU in a single-family residential zoning district from being prohibited or unreasonably restricted, but it expressly allows reasonable local rules for dimensional setbacks, bulk, height, and site-plan review. ADUs therefore do not receive a blanket exemption from local zoning dimensions. Newton's current ADU ordinance must be checked for the particular unit.

facts.text: Massachusetts prohibits municipalities from unreasonably restricting or requiring discretionary zoning approval for the single protected ADU described in Chapter 40A, Section 3.

sections.heading: What local rules may still regulate

facts.text: The statute permits reasonable regulations concerning dimensional setbacks, bulk, height, and site-plan review.
Newton publishes local ADU size, height, and setback standards for detached units.

qa.q: Does state ADU law eliminate Newton's setback rules?
qa.a: No. State law expressly allows reasonable local dimensional setback, bulk, and height regulations.
